tasks.goal: Build a small Node CLI called temp-convert that takes a temperature value and unit as argv arguments, converts between Celsius/Fahrenheit, prints the result, and exits 1 with a usage message on missing or invalid arguments, documenting success, missing-arg, and bad-value invocations with expected exit codes in a README. As a FINAL SEPARATE PHASE, run the documented invocations against the CLI and confirm stdout/stderr/exit codes match the README spec.

Create a small set of markdown files in a workspace: INGREDIENTS.md, STEPS.md, and NUTRITION.md, each describing a fictional recipe for a lentil soup. As a FINAL SEPARATE PHASE, write an INDEX.md file that links to all three documents with accurate titles and one-sentence descriptions.

Build a single-file index.html habit tracker widget with buttons to increment/decrement a daily streak counter, an input to set a goal number, and text/color styling that changes (e.g., green when goal reached, gray otherwise) based on the current streak state.

Build a single-file index.html quiz-timer widget that exposes its state via a window.__quizTimer object with getters for remaining time and running/paused status, with buttons to start, pause, and reset, and styling that changes color as time runs low. As a FINAL SEPARATE PHASE, write and run a mechanical smoke test script that drives the controls and checks the exposed state and styling change correctly.

Write and verify a no-dependency Node CLI todo-cli.js that appends a task string from argv to a local todo.txt file and lists all tasks when run with no arguments, confirming exit codes and output manually. As a FINAL SEPARATE PHASE, package this CLI by writing a package.json and a README with a 'Verified invocations' section listing the exact commands and outputs you confirmed.

Write and verify a no-dependency Node CLI slugify.js that reads a title string from process.argv[2], converts it to a lowercase hyphenated slug, prints it, and exits 1 with a stderr usage message if the argument is missing or empty.

Write a small Node HTTP server (no dependencies) in server.js implementing routes for a warehouse inventory API: GET /items, POST /items with a JSON body, and DELETE /items/:id, each returning appropriate status codes. As a FINAL SEPARATE PHASE, write a README documenting these routes, their request bodies, and status codes exactly as implemented in server.js, without probing the server live.

Write a README.md with sections Overview, Installation, and Usage, plus a CONTRIBUTING.md with sections How to Contribute and Code Style, describing a fictional static-site generator tool called Pagelet, and a config file pagelet.config.json containing the exact literal content: {"outputDir": "dist", "srcDir": "src", "port": 4000}.
